gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both entries concern the polynomial reduction from the singular-value problem to the max-angle problem, but the gold defect is failure to establish rational encoding, polynomial bit size, and a polynomial construction after spectral normalization. ISSUE-001 instead identifies an unverified m >= n hypothesis, which is a distinct assumption gap and does not recognize the encoding or bit-complexity defect.

The gold issue concerns the missing nonpositive-objective qualification in the implication from local minima to Nash pairs. ISSUE-002 concerns a separate equivalence test for whether the optimum attains +||A|| and repairs a nonnegativity condition on a 1x1 matrix; it does not diagnose the local-minimum versus Nash implication or its sign restriction.

The gold defect is treating an arbitrary, possibly nonnormalized basis V as if VV^T were the orthogonal projector, invalidating the least-squares feasibility test. ISSUE-002 addresses a different scalar extremal-value equivalence and does not recognize the basis normalization or projector operation.

The gold issue is the false spectral-radius/compressed-norm identity caused by allowing nonorthonormal bases U_G and U_H. ISSUE-001 concerns the unrelated dimension hypothesis in a reduction theorem and contains no diagnosis of the basis scaling or compressed spectral-norm formula.

The gold issue concerns nonconvex sphere-constrained AO blocks and the resulting unsupported convergence justification. ISSUE-001 concerns a dimension hypothesis in an NP-hardness reduction and has no substantive connection to the feasible-set convexity or AO convergence obligation.
